description: Conduct a structured threat modeling session for a system using STRIDE or LINDDUN, from architecture documentation through ranked threats to remediation assignments.

steps.description: Document the target system architecture, components, data flows, and external interfaces.

inputs.name: system-name
inputs.desc: Name of the system under analysis

inputs.name: architecture-sources
inputs.desc: Diagrams, docs, or code repos describing the system

inputs.name: scope-boundaries
inputs.desc: What is in and out of scope for this session

outputs.name: architecture-diagram
outputs.desc: Component and data flow diagram

outputs.name: data-flow-inventory
outputs.desc: Catalog of all data flows with classification

outputs.name: external-interfaces
outputs.desc: List of all external connections and protocols

process: Inventory all system components, services, and data stores
Map data flows between components including protocols and authentication
Identify all external interfaces, APIs, and user-facing surfaces
Document the technology stack for each component

steps.description: Identify and document trust boundaries within the system architecture.

outputs.name: trust-boundary-map
outputs.desc: Diagram with trust boundaries marked

outputs.name: boundary-crossing-inventory
outputs.desc: All data flows that cross trust boundaries

outputs.name: privilege-level-map
outputs.desc: Privilege levels on each side of each boundary

process: Identify network boundaries (public internet, DMZ, internal, database tier)
Identify process boundaries (user space, kernel, container, VM)
Identify privilege transitions (anonymous to authenticated, user to admin)
Document each data flow that crosses a trust boundary

steps.description: Enumerate threats at each trust boundary crossing using the STRIDE classification.

outputs.name: threat-catalog
outputs.desc: Full list of identified threats with STRIDE category

outputs.name: attack-trees
outputs.desc: Attack tree diagrams for high-complexity threats

process: For each boundary crossing, enumerate Spoofing threats to identity
Enumerate Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, Denial of Service, and Elevation of Privilege threats
Build attack trees for threats that involve multiple steps
Cross-reference with known vulnerability patterns for the technology stack

steps.description: Rank each identified threat by likelihood and impact to prioritize remediation.

inputs.name: attack-trees
inputs.desc: Attack tree diagrams for complex threats

outputs.name: ranked-threat-list
outputs.desc: Threats ordered by risk score (likelihood times impact)

outputs.name: risk-matrix
outputs.desc: Visual risk matrix mapping threats to likelihood and impact

process: Score each threat for likelihood (attacker skill, access required, tooling availability)
Score each threat for impact (confidentiality, integrity, availability, financial, regulatory)
Compute risk as likelihood times impact
Plot threats on the risk matrix and sort by descending risk

steps.description: Map existing security controls to each threat and identify coverage gaps.

outputs.name: mitigation-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Each threat paired with its existing mitigations

outputs.name: gap-list
outputs.desc: Threats with no mitigation or insufficient coverage

process: Inventory existing security controls (firewalls, WAF, authentication, encryption, monitoring)
Map each control to the threats it addresses
Assess whether each control sufficiently reduces the risk
Flag threats with no mitigation or partial mitigation as gaps

steps.description: Assign remediation actions for each gap to owners with timelines.

inputs.name: gap-list
inputs.desc: Threats with no or insufficient mitigation

outputs.name: remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of remediation actions with owners and deadlines

outputs.name: residual-risk-summary
outputs.desc: Expected risk posture after remediation

process: For each gap, propose one or more remediation options with cost estimates
Assign each remediation to an owner (team or individual)
Set timelines based on risk priority (critical within 30 days, high within 90 days)
Calculate the residual risk assuming remediation succeeds

steps.description: Compile all findings into the final threat model document.

outputs.name: threat-model-document
outputs.desc: Complete threat model document with all sections

outputs.name: executive-summary
outputs.desc: One-page summary of critical findings and next steps

process: Assemble the document with architecture, trust boundaries, threat catalog, risk matrix, and remediation plan
Write the executive summary highlighting the top five risks and their status
Include appendices with full threat catalog and attack trees
Set the review cadence (re-run threat model when architecture changes)

description: Plan and execute a red team exercise from scoping and OSINT through attack execution to blue team debrief and final report.

steps.description: Define the objectives, rules of engagement, and scope for the red team exercise.

inputs.name: target-description
inputs.desc: Description of the target organization or system

inputs.name: stakeholder-goals
inputs.desc: What the exercise should test or prove

inputs.name: legal-authorization
inputs.desc: Signed authorization and rules of engagement

outputs.name: scope-document
outputs.desc: Formal scope with in-scope and out-of-scope targets

outputs.name: rules-of-engagement
outputs.desc: Constraints, communication protocols, and emergency stop procedures

process: Interview stakeholders to define success criteria
Enumerate in-scope systems, networks, and personnel
Define out-of-scope items and prohibited techniques
Establish communication channels and emergency stop procedures

steps.description: Gather open-source intelligence on the target to inform attack planning.

outputs.name: osint-report
outputs.desc: Collected intelligence organized by category

outputs.name: attack-surface-map
outputs.desc: External-facing assets, domains, IPs, and services discovered

process: Enumerate domains, subdomains, and IP ranges from DNS and certificate transparency logs
Collect employee names, roles, and email formats from public sources
Identify exposed services, technologies, and version information
Map the external attack surface and note potential entry points

steps.description: Develop the attack plan with specific techniques, tools, and phases.

outputs.name: attack-plan
outputs.desc: Phased attack plan with techniques mapped to MITRE ATT&CK

outputs.name: tooling-list
outputs.desc: Tools and infrastructure required for each phase

process: Map potential attack paths from initial access through objectives
Select techniques for each phase and map to MITRE ATT&CK framework
Prepare custom tooling and infrastructure (C2, phishing domains, payloads)
Define fallback techniques if primary approaches are detected or blocked

steps.description: Execute the attack plan with detailed logging of every action and finding.

outputs.name: operation-log
outputs.desc: Timestamped log of every action taken and result observed

outputs.name: findings-list
outputs.desc: Vulnerabilities and weaknesses exploited with evidence

process: Execute initial access attempts (phishing, external exploit, credential stuffing)
Perform lateral movement and privilege escalation if initial access succeeds
Attempt to achieve defined objectives (data access, domain admin, critical system compromise)
Log every action with timestamps, screenshots, and packet captures

steps.description: Monitor and maintain operational security throughout the exercise.

outputs.name: opsec-assessment
outputs.desc: Assessment of whether the operation was detected at each stage

outputs.name: detection-timeline
outputs.desc: When the blue team detected activity, if at all

process: Track which actions generated alerts in the target environment
Monitor for blue team response actions (IP blocks, account locks, incident tickets)
Assess whether the operation remained covert through each phase
Document the detection timeline for comparison with blue team records

steps.description: Conduct a collaborative debrief between the red and blue teams.

outputs.name: debrief-notes
outputs.desc: Notes from the joint debrief session

outputs.name: improvement-recommendations
outputs.desc: Agreed-upon improvements for detection and response

process: Walk through the attack timeline with the blue team
Compare red team actions with blue team alerts and responses
Identify detection gaps and response delays
Agree on prioritized improvements for detection, prevention, and response

steps.description: Compile the final red team exercise report with findings, evidence, and recommendations.

outputs.name: red-team-report
outputs.desc: Complete red team exercise report with executive summary

outputs.name: remediation-tracker
outputs.desc: Tracking table for each finding with owner and deadline

process: Write the executive summary with key findings and overall risk assessment
Detail each finding with evidence, impact, and recommended remediation
Include the attack narrative from initial access through objectives
Build the remediation tracker with severity, owner, and target date for each item

description: Handle a vulnerability disclosure from initial report through validation, fix coordination, and public advisory.

steps.description: Receive and acknowledge a vulnerability report, and perform initial triage.

inputs.name: product-inventory
inputs.desc: List of products and versions in scope

outputs.name: triage-record
outputs.desc: Initial triage with affected product, severity estimate, and status

outputs.name: acknowledgment-sent
outputs.desc: Confirmation that the reporter received acknowledgment

process: Log the report with a tracking identifier and timestamp
Send acknowledgment to the reporter within 24 hours
Perform initial triage to identify affected product and version
Assign to the appropriate security engineer for validation

steps.description: Reproduce and validate the reported vulnerability in a controlled environment.

inputs.name: vulnerability-report
inputs.desc: The original report with reproduction steps

outputs.name: reproduction-result
outputs.desc: Whether the vulnerability was confirmed, with proof

outputs.name: affected-versions
outputs.desc: List of all product versions affected

process: Set up the test environment matching reported conditions
Follow the reporter's reproduction steps exactly
If reproduction fails, request additional details from the reporter
Test across other versions and configurations to determine full scope

steps.description: Score the confirmed vulnerability using CVSS and classify its severity.

outputs.name: cvss-score
outputs.desc: CVSS base, temporal, and environmental scores

outputs.name: severity-classification
outputs.desc: Critical, High, Medium, or Low classification

process: Score the CVSS base metrics (attack vector, complexity, privileges required, user interaction, scope, CIA impact)
Score temporal metrics (exploit maturity, remediation level, report confidence)
Classify severity based on the overall score
Compare with similar past vulnerabilities for consistency

steps.description: Coordinate the fix with engineering, including timeline and testing.

outputs.name: fix-branch
outputs.desc: Code fix ready for review and merge

outputs.name: fix-timeline
outputs.desc: Dates for fix completion, testing, and release

process: Brief the engineering team on the vulnerability without disclosing publicly
Set the fix deadline based on severity (critical: 7 days, high: 30 days, medium: 90 days)
Review and test the proposed fix for completeness and regression
Verify the fix eliminates the vulnerability across all affected versions

steps.description: Prepare the security advisory with CVE assignment and mitigation guidance.

outputs.name: security-advisory
outputs.desc: Public advisory text with CVE, description, affected versions, and fix

outputs.name: cve-id
outputs.desc: Assigned CVE identifier

process: Request a CVE identifier from the appropriate CNA
Write the advisory with description, impact, affected versions, and remediation
Include workarounds for users who cannot apply the fix immediately
Set the advisory publication date to align with fix availability

steps.description: Notify affected parties including downstream vendors, customers, and the reporter.

outputs.name: notification-log
outputs.desc: Record of all parties notified with dates

outputs.name: reporter-update
outputs.desc: Final update sent to the reporter

process: Notify the reporter of the fix and advisory date, offer credit
Notify downstream vendors and partners under embargo if needed
Prepare customer notification for the release date
Coordinate with CERT/CC or other coordinators if the scope is broad

steps.description: Publish the advisory and disclosure timeline.

outputs.name: published-advisory
outputs.desc: The advisory as published on the security page

outputs.name: disclosure-timeline
outputs.desc: Full timeline from report to publication

process: Publish the advisory on the product security page and mailing lists
Update the CVE record with final details
Publish the disclosure timeline including all key dates
Archive the complete case file for future reference

description: Test data loss prevention controls across network, endpoint, and cloud exfiltration channels with detection and response time measurement.

steps.description: Classify the data types in scope for exfiltration testing.

inputs.name: data-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of data stores and types in the environment

inputs.name: test-scope
inputs.desc: Which systems and data types are in scope

outputs.name: test-data-set
outputs.desc: Synthetic test data matching each classification level

outputs.name: classification-matrix
outputs.desc: Data types mapped to sensitivity levels and expected controls

process: Review the data classification policy and identify all sensitivity levels
Create synthetic test data that matches each level (PII, financial, health, IP, credentials)
Map each data type to the DLP controls that should detect it
Prepare test payloads in multiple formats (plain text, encoded, compressed, encrypted)

steps.description: Test network-based exfiltration channels including HTTP, DNS, and ICMP tunneling.

outputs.name: network-test-results
outputs.desc: Pass/fail for each network exfiltration channel tested

outputs.name: network-detection-times
outputs.desc: Time from exfiltration attempt to alert for each test

process: Test HTTP/HTTPS exfiltration to external endpoints (direct upload, webmail, paste sites)
Test DNS tunneling by encoding data in DNS queries to a controlled domain
Test ICMP tunneling and other protocol covert channels
Record whether each attempt was blocked, alerted, or passed undetected

steps.description: Test endpoint-based exfiltration channels including USB, print, and clipboard.

outputs.name: endpoint-test-results
outputs.desc: Pass/fail for each endpoint exfiltration channel

outputs.name: endpoint-detection-times
outputs.desc: Time from attempt to alert for each test

process: Test USB device write with classified data (mass storage, phone, camera)
Test print to physical and virtual printers with classified content
Test clipboard copy between controlled and uncontrolled applications
Test screen capture and screen sharing with classified data on screen

steps.description: Test cloud-based exfiltration channels including sync services and email attachments.

outputs.name: cloud-test-results
outputs.desc: Pass/fail for each cloud exfiltration channel

outputs.name: cloud-detection-times
outputs.desc: Time from attempt to alert for each test

process: Test file sync services (personal cloud storage, unauthorized SaaS applications)
Test email attachments to external addresses with classified content
Test cloud storage API uploads from corporate endpoints
Test data sharing through collaboration tools to external accounts

steps.description: Test whether DLP controls can inspect or flag encrypted exfiltration channels.

outputs.name: encryption-test-results
outputs.desc: Pass/fail for detection of encrypted exfiltration

outputs.name: ssl-inspection-gaps
outputs.desc: Encrypted channels that bypass inspection

process: Test exfiltration over TLS to non-standard ports
Test exfiltration through certificate-pinned applications that resist inspection
Test steganographic embedding in images or documents sent through approved channels
Identify which encrypted channels are inspected and which bypass DLP

steps.description: Measure and analyze detection and response times across all exfiltration tests.

outputs.name: response-time-analysis
outputs.desc: Statistical summary of detection and response times

outputs.name: coverage-gap-summary
outputs.desc: Channels with no detection or slow detection

process: Compute mean, median, and 95th percentile detection times per channel
Identify channels with zero detection (complete gaps)
Categorize gaps by severity (blocked, alerted, logged only, undetected)
Rank improvements by the volume of data at risk through each gap

steps.description: Produce the final DLP assessment report with findings and recommendations.

outputs.name: dlp-assessment-report
outputs.desc: Complete DLP assessment report

outputs.name: remediation-priorities
outputs.desc: Ranked list of control improvements needed

process: Summarize test coverage across all channels and data types
Detail each gap with the test evidence and risk implication
Recommend specific control improvements for each gap
Estimate the cost and timeline for each remediation

description: Audit the security posture of a Kubernetes cluster from control plane configuration through RBAC, pod security, network policies, and runtime protections.

steps.description: Audit the Kubernetes control plane configuration for security misconfigurations.

inputs.name: cluster-access
inputs.desc: Kubeconfig or access credentials for the cluster

inputs.name: cluster-version
inputs.desc: Kubernetes version and distribution (EKS, GKE, AKS, self-managed)

inputs.name: audit-scope
inputs.desc: Which namespaces and components are in scope

outputs.name: control-plane-findings
outputs.desc: Misconfigurations in API server, etcd, scheduler, and controller manager

outputs.name: cluster-inventory
outputs.desc: Inventory of namespaces, nodes, pods, and services

process: Check API server flags (anonymous auth, RBAC mode, audit logging, admission controllers)
Verify etcd encryption at rest and access controls
Check scheduler and controller manager for insecure settings
Compare against CIS Kubernetes Benchmark

steps.description: Review RBAC policies, service accounts, and privilege assignments.

inputs.name: cluster-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of namespaces, pods, and services

outputs.name: rbac-findings
outputs.desc: Over-privileged roles, risky bindings, and unused service accounts

outputs.name: privilege-map
outputs.desc: Map of which identities can do what across namespaces

process: Enumerate all ClusterRoles, Roles, ClusterRoleBindings, and RoleBindings
Identify roles with wildcard permissions or access to secrets
Check for default service account tokens mounted in pods
Flag service accounts with cluster-admin or equivalent privileges

steps.description: Check pod security standards, admission controllers, and container configurations.

inputs.name: control-plane-findings
inputs.desc: API server and admission controller status

outputs.name: pod-security-findings
outputs.desc: Pods running as root, with host access, or without security context

outputs.name: admission-controller-status
outputs.desc: Which admission controllers are active and their policies

process: Check for pods running as root or with privileged containers
Identify pods with hostNetwork, hostPID, hostIPC, or host path mounts
Verify Pod Security Standards enforcement (baseline, restricted)
Check for missing security contexts (readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities drop)

steps.description: Test network policies and verify network segmentation between pods and namespaces.

inputs.name: cluster-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of namespaces, pods, and services

outputs.name: network-policy-findings
outputs.desc: Missing or overly permissive network policies

outputs.name: network-reachability-map
outputs.desc: Which pods can communicate with which other pods

process: Enumerate all NetworkPolicy resources across namespaces
Identify namespaces with no network policies (default allow-all)
Test actual connectivity between pods in different namespaces
Verify that egress policies restrict outbound traffic to needed destinations only

steps.description: Verify that secrets are encrypted at rest and properly managed.

outputs.name: secrets-findings
outputs.desc: Secrets stored unencrypted, exposed in env vars, or logged

outputs.name: secrets-management-status
outputs.desc: Whether external secrets managers are used and configured correctly

process: Check EncryptionConfiguration for etcd encryption at rest
Identify secrets passed as environment variables instead of mounted volumes
Check for secrets exposed in container logs or pod specs
Verify integration with external secrets managers (Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault)

steps.description: Review runtime security controls including seccomp, AppArmor, and container image policies.

outputs.name: runtime-security-findings
outputs.desc: Missing or weak runtime security controls

outputs.name: image-policy-status
outputs.desc: Whether image signing and scanning are enforced

process: Check for seccomp profiles applied to pods
Check for AppArmor or SELinux profiles on containers
Verify that image pull policies prevent use of unsigned or unscanned images
Check for runtime monitoring tools and their coverage

steps.description: Compile all findings into the Kubernetes security audit report.

outputs.name: k8s-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete Kubernetes security audit report

outputs.name: hardening-checklist
outputs.desc: Prioritized checklist of hardening actions

process: Organize findings by severity and category
Write the executive summary with critical and high severity counts
Produce the hardening checklist with specific remediation steps for each finding
Include CIS Benchmark compliance percentage and gap analysis

description: Review serverless function security across IAM roles, event triggers, environment handling, and function-to-function trust boundaries.

steps.description: Inventory all serverless functions, their triggers, and runtime configurations.

inputs.name: cloud-account-access
inputs.desc: Credentials or role for the cloud account

inputs.name: review-scope
inputs.desc: Which regions, accounts, or projects to include

outputs.name: function-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete list of functions with runtime, memory, timeout, and trigger type

outputs.name: trigger-map
outputs.desc: Map of event sources to functions they invoke

process: Enumerate all functions across regions and accounts
Record runtime version, memory allocation, timeout, and environment variables
Map all event sources (API Gateway, S3, SQS, SNS, EventBridge, schedule) to their functions
Identify functions that invoke other functions directly

steps.description: Check IAM execution roles for least privilege violations.

inputs.name: function-inventory
inputs.desc: List of functions with their roles

outputs.name: iam-findings
outputs.desc: Over-privileged roles, wildcard permissions, and unused permissions

outputs.name: least-privilege-recommendations
outputs.desc: Tightened IAM policies for each function

process: Extract the IAM policy for each function's execution role
Identify wildcard resource or action permissions
Compare granted permissions against actually used permissions (via CloudTrail or equivalent)
Flag roles that grant access to resources outside the function's need

steps.description: Test each trigger type for event injection vulnerabilities.

outputs.name: injection-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of event injection attempts per trigger type

outputs.name: input-validation-gaps
outputs.desc: Functions that do not validate event payloads

process: Craft malicious payloads for each trigger type (SQL injection in API Gateway, path traversal in S3 keys)
Test whether functions validate and sanitize event data before processing
Test for deserialization vulnerabilities in event parsing
Check whether error messages leak internal details

steps.description: Review environment variable handling for secrets exposure.

outputs.name: env-var-findings
outputs.desc: Secrets in plaintext env vars, unencrypted, or logged

outputs.name: secrets-handling-status
outputs.desc: Whether functions use secrets managers instead of env vars

process: List all environment variables per function and classify their contents
Identify secrets stored as plaintext environment variables
Check whether environment variables are encrypted with KMS
Verify that secrets are not logged during function execution

steps.description: Test for cold start abuse, timeout manipulation, and resource exhaustion.

inputs.name: function-inventory
inputs.desc: Function configurations with timeout and memory

outputs.name: abuse-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of abuse and resource exhaustion tests

outputs.name: concurrency-limits-status
outputs.desc: Whether concurrency limits are set per function

process: Test whether functions can be invoked at a rate that exhausts concurrency limits
Check for timeout configurations that allow long-running abuse
Test whether recursive or circular invocations are possible
Verify that per-function concurrency limits and reserved capacity are set

steps.description: Test function-to-function trust boundaries and inter-function authentication.

outputs.name: trust-boundary-findings
outputs.desc: Missing authentication between functions and implicit trust issues

outputs.name: inter-function-map
outputs.desc: Map of which functions call which and how they authenticate

process: Trace all function-to-function invocations
Test whether calling functions authenticate to called functions
Check for shared IAM roles across functions that should be isolated
Verify that event payloads between functions are validated at each boundary

steps.description: Compile the serverless security review report.

outputs.name: serverless-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete serverless security review report

outputs.name: remediation-actions
outputs.desc: Prioritized list of fixes with implementation guidance

process: Organize findings by severity across all test categories
Write the executive summary with risk posture assessment
Detail each finding with evidence, impact, and remediation steps
Produce the remediation action list with priority and effort estimates

description: Assess Active Directory security from domain enumeration through Kerberoasting, delegation, and Group Policy analysis.

steps.description: Enumerate the Active Directory domain structure, trusts, and organizational units.

inputs.name: assessment-scope
inputs.desc: Which domains and forests are in scope

outputs.name: domain-structure
outputs.desc: Forest, domain, trust, and OU hierarchy

outputs.name: account-inventory
outputs.desc: Users, groups, computers, and service accounts

process: Enumerate the forest structure, all domains, and trust relationships
Map organizational units and their linked Group Policy Objects
Inventory all user accounts, computer accounts, and service accounts
Identify trust types (forest, external, realm) and their direction and transitivity

steps.description: Check for Kerberoastable service accounts with weak passwords.

outputs.name: kerberoastable-accounts
outputs.desc: Service accounts with SPNs and their cracking results

outputs.name: asrep-roastable-accounts
outputs.desc: Accounts with pre-authentication disabled

process: Query for all accounts with registered Service Principal Names
Request TGS tickets for each Kerberoastable account
Attempt offline cracking of the ticket hashes
Query for accounts with Kerberos pre-authentication disabled and attempt AS-REP roasting

steps.description: Identify over-privileged accounts and dangerous group memberships.

outputs.name: privilege-findings
outputs.desc: Over-privileged accounts, nested group escalation paths, and stale admin accounts

outputs.name: attack-path-map
outputs.desc: Paths from low-privilege accounts to domain admin

process: Enumerate members of Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, and all privileged groups
Trace nested group memberships to find hidden privilege paths
Identify accounts with AdminCount=1 that are not in privileged groups (orphaned admin SDProp)
Map attack paths from standard user to domain admin using ACL analysis

steps.description: Check for unconstrained and constrained delegation misconfigurations.

outputs.name: delegation-findings
outputs.desc: Accounts with unconstrained, constrained, or resource-based constrained delegation

outputs.name: delegation-risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Risk rating for each delegation configuration

process: Query for all objects with unconstrained delegation enabled
Query for objects with constrained delegation and their allowed target services
Check for resource-based constrained delegation configurations
Assess whether each delegation setting creates an exploitable path to high-value targets

steps.description: Analyze Group Policy Objects for security settings and misconfigurations.

outputs.name: gpo-findings
outputs.desc: Weak GPO settings, password policy gaps, and audit policy gaps

outputs.name: gpo-security-baseline-comparison
outputs.desc: Comparison of current settings against Microsoft security baselines

process: Export and analyze all GPO settings (password policy, lockout, audit, user rights assignments)
Compare password and lockout policies against current best practices
Check audit policies for coverage of logon events, privilege use, and object access
Compare against Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit baselines

steps.description: Compile the Active Directory security assessment report.

outputs.name: ad-security-report
outputs.desc: Complete Active Directory security assessment report

outputs.name: ad-remediation-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized remediation actions with implementation guidance

process: Rank findings by exploitability and impact
Write the executive summary with the most critical attack paths
Detail each finding with reproduction steps and evidence
Produce the remediation plan with quick wins, medium-term fixes, and long-term improvements

description: Assess organizational readiness against ransomware across backup integrity, network segmentation, endpoint detection, initial access vectors, and incident response.

steps.description: Test backup integrity, isolation, and recovery time for critical systems.

inputs.name: backup-inventory
inputs.desc: Inventory of backup systems and schedules

inputs.name: critical-systems-list
inputs.desc: List of systems critical to business operations

inputs.name: rto-rpo-targets
inputs.desc: Recovery time and recovery point objectives

outputs.name: backup-test-results
outputs.desc: Restore success/failure for each system with actual recovery time

outputs.name: backup-isolation-status
outputs.desc: Whether backups are isolated from the production network

process: Verify that backups exist and are current for all critical systems
Test restore of each backup type (full, incremental, snapshot) to an isolated environment
Measure actual recovery time and compare against RTO targets
Verify that backup infrastructure is isolated and not reachable from the production domain

steps.description: Test network segmentation to assess how far ransomware could spread laterally.

inputs.name: critical-systems-list
inputs.desc: Critical systems and their network locations

outputs.name: segmentation-test-results
outputs.desc: Which systems are reachable from a compromised workstation

outputs.name: lateral-movement-paths
outputs.desc: Paths from user workstation tier to server and backup tiers

process: From a standard workstation, test connectivity to all network segments
Identify which ports and services are reachable across segment boundaries
Test whether administrative protocols (RDP, SMB, WinRM) are restricted between tiers
Map the blast radius from a single compromised endpoint

steps.description: Verify endpoint detection and response coverage and effectiveness.

outputs.name: edr-coverage-findings
outputs.desc: Systems missing EDR agents and detection gaps

outputs.name: detection-test-results
outputs.desc: Results of simulated ransomware behavior detection

process: Verify EDR agent deployment across all endpoints including servers and VMs
Test detection of common ransomware behaviors (mass file encryption, shadow copy deletion, registry changes)
Check for EDR exclusions that could be abused to evade detection
Verify that alerts reach the SOC and that response playbooks exist

steps.description: Test common ransomware initial access vectors (phishing, RDP, VPN).

outputs.name: initial-access-results
outputs.desc: Test results for each initial access vector

outputs.name: exposed-services-inventory
outputs.desc: Internet-exposed services and their patch status

process: Test email gateway filtering of common ransomware delivery methods (malicious macros, ISO attachments, HTML smuggling)
Check for internet-exposed RDP, SMB, and other management protocols
Test VPN and remote access for default credentials and known vulnerabilities
Verify patch status of internet-facing services

steps.description: Check administrative credential hygiene and privileged access management.

inputs.name: network-architecture
inputs.desc: Network tiers and admin access patterns

outputs.name: credential-hygiene-findings
outputs.desc: Shared admin accounts, stale credentials, and missing MFA

outputs.name: pam-status
outputs.desc: Privileged access management coverage and configuration

process: Check for shared local administrator passwords across endpoints
Verify MFA enforcement on all administrative access paths
Check for service accounts with interactive logon rights and non-rotating passwords
Assess privileged access workstation and tiered administration compliance

steps.description: Test the ransomware incident response plan through a tabletop exercise.

outputs.name: tabletop-results
outputs.desc: Gaps and delays identified during the tabletop exercise

outputs.name: plan-readiness-score
outputs.desc: Overall readiness score with category breakdowns

process: Run a ransomware scenario tabletop exercise with the IR team
Time key decisions (contain, notify, pay/no-pay, restore) and identify bottlenecks
Check whether communication plans and contact lists are current
Assess whether the team can execute the response without external help within the target timeline

steps.description: Produce the ransomware readiness assessment report.

outputs.name: ransomware-readiness-report
outputs.desc: Complete ransomware readiness assessment report

outputs.name: improvement-roadmap
outputs.desc: Prioritized roadmap of improvements with timeline and cost

process: Score readiness across all categories (prevention, detection, response, recovery)
Summarize the critical gaps that would determine the outcome of a real attack
Produce the improvement roadmap with quick wins, 30-day, 90-day, and 180-day milestones
Include a cost-benefit comparison of improvements against estimated ransomware impact

description: Review zero trust architecture implementation across identity verification, device posture, microsegmentation, continuous authorization, and legacy bypass detection.

steps.description: Map all access flows and verify identity checks at each step.

inputs.name: review-scope
inputs.desc: Systems and access patterns to review

outputs.name: access-flow-map
outputs.desc: Every access flow with identity verification points marked

outputs.name: identity-gap-list
outputs.desc: Access flows missing identity verification

process: Trace each user, service, and device access flow from request to resource
Verify that identity is checked at every step (not just at the perimeter)
Identify flows that rely on network location instead of identity for access decisions
Flag service-to-service communications that lack mutual authentication

steps.description: Test whether device posture is enforced as a condition of access.

inputs.name: access-flow-map
inputs.desc: All access flows with identity checks

outputs.name: posture-enforcement-results
outputs.desc: Which access flows check device posture and which do not

outputs.name: posture-bypass-paths
outputs.desc: Ways to access resources from non-compliant devices

process: Test access from a compliant enrolled device and confirm success
Test access from a non-compliant device (missing patches, no encryption, no MDM) and confirm denial
Test access from an unmanaged personal device
Identify access paths that skip device posture checks entirely

steps.description: Verify microsegmentation between workloads and services.

outputs.name: microsegmentation-findings
outputs.desc: Workloads that can communicate when they should not

outputs.name: segmentation-coverage-map
outputs.desc: Map of enforced vs unenforced segment boundaries

process: Test connectivity between workloads that should be isolated
Verify that microsegmentation policies match the intended design
Check for flat network segments where all workloads can reach all others
Test whether segmentation is enforced at the application layer, not just the network layer

steps.description: Test continuous authentication and authorization during active sessions.

outputs.name: continuous-auth-findings
outputs.desc: Sessions that persist after posture or risk changes

outputs.name: session-lifetime-analysis
outputs.desc: Session durations and re-authentication frequency

process: Establish a session, then change the device posture to non-compliant and check if access is revoked
Test whether disabling the user account terminates active sessions
Check session token lifetimes and whether step-up authentication triggers on sensitive actions
Test whether risk-based policies adjust access during an active session

steps.description: Detect implicit trust assumptions in the architecture.

outputs.name: implicit-trust-findings
outputs.desc: Places where network location, source IP, or VPN connection grants access without identity

outputs.name: trust-assumption-inventory
outputs.desc: Complete catalog of trust assumptions in the architecture

process: Identify resources accessible solely because the requester is on the corporate network
Test for VPN split-tunnel configurations that expose internal resources
Check for API endpoints that trust caller identity based on source IP rather than authentication
Catalog every place where access is granted by something other than verified identity and context

steps.description: Find legacy systems and configurations that bypass zero trust controls.

outputs.name: legacy-bypass-findings
outputs.desc: Legacy systems, protocols, and configurations that bypass zero trust

outputs.name: migration-priority-list
outputs.desc: Priority order for migrating or isolating legacy bypasses

process: Identify systems using legacy protocols that cannot participate in zero trust (NTLM, telnet, FTP)
Find VPN or remote access paths that grant broad network access
Check for firewall rules that pre-date the zero trust implementation and are still active
Prioritize each bypass by the sensitivity of the resources it exposes

steps.description: Compile the zero trust architecture review report.

outputs.name: zero-trust-review-report
outputs.desc: Complete zero trust architecture review report

outputs.name: zero-trust-maturity-score
outputs.desc: Maturity score across zero trust pillars with improvement plan

process: Score the implementation against zero trust maturity model pillars (identity, device, network, application, data)
Summarize findings by pillar with severity rankings
Produce the improvement plan with priorities based on risk reduction per effort
Include a roadmap from current state to target zero trust maturity level

description: Assess security risk from third-party integrations across vendor certifications, API security, data handling, access controls, and business continuity.

steps.description: Inventory all third-party vendor connections and data sharing agreements.

inputs.name: vendor-list
inputs.desc: List of third-party vendors and service providers

inputs.name: contract-repository
inputs.desc: Vendor contracts and data processing agreements

inputs.name: assessment-scope
inputs.desc: Which vendors and integrations to assess

outputs.name: integration-inventory
outputs.desc: All vendor connections with data types shared, protocols, and access methods

outputs.name: data-sharing-matrix
outputs.desc: Matrix of which data goes to which vendor and why

process: Catalog every vendor integration including APIs, file transfers, and shared databases
Document the data types shared with each vendor and the legal basis
Identify which vendors have access to production environments
Map the authentication and authorization methods for each integration

steps.description: Review vendor security certifications, audit reports, and compliance documentation.

outputs.name: certification-status
outputs.desc: SOC2, ISO 27001, and other certifications with expiry dates and scope

outputs.name: audit-findings-summary
outputs.desc: Notable findings from vendor audit reports

process: Collect current SOC2 Type II reports, ISO 27001 certificates, and other relevant certifications
Verify that certification scope covers the services you use
Review audit report findings and management responses
Flag vendors missing certifications or with expired reports

steps.description: Test the security of API integrations with each vendor.

outputs.name: api-security-findings
outputs.desc: Authentication, authorization, encryption, and input validation issues

outputs.name: api-risk-ratings
outputs.desc: Risk rating for each vendor API integration

process: Test authentication mechanisms (API keys, OAuth, mTLS) for each integration
Verify that data in transit is encrypted with current TLS versions
Test for authorization bypass (accessing other tenants' data, horizontal privilege escalation)
Check rate limiting and error handling for information disclosure

steps.description: Check how vendors handle, store, and protect your data.

inputs.name: data-sharing-matrix
inputs.desc: Data types shared with each vendor

outputs.name: data-handling-findings
outputs.desc: Issues with vendor data storage, encryption, retention, and deletion

outputs.name: data-residency-status
outputs.desc: Where each vendor stores your data geographically

process: Verify that vendors encrypt your data at rest and document the encryption method
Check data retention policies and confirm vendors delete data when required
Verify data residency complies with your regulatory requirements
Check whether vendors use your data for purposes beyond the contract (training ML models, analytics)

steps.description: Review vendor access to your environment and the controls around it.

outputs.name: vendor-access-findings
outputs.desc: Over-privileged vendor accounts, shared credentials, and missing audit trails

outputs.name: access-control-recommendations
outputs.desc: Recommended access restrictions for each vendor

process: Inventory all vendor accounts, API keys, and access credentials in your environment
Check whether vendor access follows least privilege
Verify that vendor access is logged and auditable
Test whether vendor credentials can be used outside their intended scope

steps.description: Assess business continuity risk from vendor dependency and potential failure.

inputs.name: vendor-list
inputs.desc: Vendor list with financial and operational details

outputs.name: continuity-risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Business impact of each vendor failing or being compromised

outputs.name: contingency-plan-status
outputs.desc: Whether contingency plans exist for critical vendor dependencies

process: Classify each vendor by criticality to business operations
Assess the business impact if each critical vendor becomes unavailable
Check for concentration risk (multiple dependencies on one vendor)
Verify that contingency plans and data portability options exist for critical vendors

steps.description: Compile the third-party risk assessment report.

outputs.name: third-party-risk-report
outputs.desc: Complete third-party risk assessment report

outputs.name: vendor-risk-register
outputs.desc: Risk register with each vendor's risk rating and required actions

process: Rate each vendor on a risk scale based on data sensitivity, access level, and security posture
Write the executive summary with the highest-risk vendors highlighted
Detail each finding with the affected vendor, evidence, and recommended action
Produce the vendor risk register with review cadence for each risk tier
